Selecting the appropriate user identity has a great impact on improving the accuracy of user behavior analysis, especially the funnel, retention, Session and other user\-related analysis functions. Therefore, before any data access, it is necessary to determine how to identify the user.

<span id="49a2835c"></span>
# Basic concept

BytePlus DataFinder uses device_id, user_unique_id, and ssid IDs to identify devices and users.

<span id="d83638ff"></span>
## Device_id/web_id/anonymous_id

The system generates a unique identifier for each device through the device registration service according to the obtained device information, which will be stored locally on the device through the client side SDK. Generally, App products will use the concept, such as Android phones, iOS phones, iPads, web terminals, Mini Program web_id, the role is basically the same as device_id.


|**Device unique identifier type** |**Data type** |**Introduction to Generative Logic** |**Features/Limitations** |
|---|---|---|---|
|device_id |int |If it is a new device will generate a new device_id, if it is an existing device will issue an existing device_id, so you can do different apps on the same device can use the same device_id. |High coverage, low conflict rate, low drift rate, high stability, correlatable data, and does not support business customization, subject to SDK acquisition. |
|web_id |int |Generated by app_id (volcano application id), the current URL, the referer of the URL, the useragent of the current browser, and user_unique_id (usually null), the Mini Program side is mainly generated by app_id (volcano application id) because there is no browser information such as URL. |null |
|anonymous_id |string |Use anonymous_id if you want to report the device unique identity generated by your server level/client side.<br><br>device_id, web_id is usually reported by the client side after the DataFinder is generated. When using anonymous_id, the client side will report the unique device identifier generated by the client side as anonymous_id while reporting the device_id and web_id. |* SaaS\-cloud native environments support use.<br><br>* In a privatized environment, if the unified ID service has been turned on, it can be used directly; if not, you need to contact the technical support staff for configuration, and it can be used after completion.<br><br>* iOS client side, Android client side does not support reporting anonymous_id. |


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-tips-is-title="true">tip</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">device_id, web_id, anonymous_id can be used as the unique id of the device, similar to the use of the following logical introduction, logical examples are device_id as an example, similar usage web_id, anonymous_id.</div>


<span id="51feb96f"></span>
## **user_unique_id**

User unique identity, generally directly using the user identity used in the product business, such as login account. When the user_unique_id is not set, in the SaaS version, the system will automatically use device_id/web_id replacement, in the privatization version, it will be displayed as empty.

<span id="7b0b8f18"></span>
## **ssid**

BytePlus DataFinder **The default statistical caliber ID used (that is, the default user ID statistical caliber of DataFinder is ssid)**  , and the device identification device_id/web_id, login state user identification user_unique_id Mapping each other, can ensure the user anonymity and real\-name state ID unity. The id_mapping logic in each environment is slightly different:


* In the SaaS\-cloud native and privatized environment, in the scenario of **enabling unified ID service** , id_mapping is isolated according to group granularity (one principal is defaulted within the group). For detailed logic id_mapping, please refer to the following **Identifying User Logic: Global Association (Logical Upgrade)**  .


**The main functions of SSID are:** 


* You can track the behavior of a user before and after registering (logging in) on a device, and will not be repeatedly recorded as a new user because of the login behavior.

* You can get through the behavior of a registered user after logging in on different devices.

* It can solve the problem of user behavior attribution for multiple accounts logged in on the same device.


<span id="f480ecbd"></span>
# ssid identity logic

<span id="e0f2b934"></span>
## New and old ssid logo logic


|**Breakdown comparison** |**Simple Association (Legacy Logic)**  |**Global Association (Logical Upgrade)**  |
|---|---|---|
|User id association logic |<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," /><br><br><br>* Ssid is generated by device_id/web_id and user_unique_id, cross\-referenced between device_id/web_id and user_unique_id, user_unique_id priority is greater than device_id/web_id<br><br>* When generating the ssid, the relationship between the individual IDs is bound.<br><br>   * The relationship between device_id/web_id and ssid is n: n, through device_id/web_id can only find the ssid of the latest binding of the id, and through ssid can only find the device_id/web_id of the latest binding of the ssid<br><br>   * There is a 1:1 relationship between user_unique_id and ssid |<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," /><br><br>Through the independent unified ID service, it provides ID generation function for the products in the marketing suite, and realizes multi\-caliber and multi\-subject ID unification on the basis of satisfying the old version of the scene.<br><br><br>* Ssid is generated by device_id/web_id and user_unique_id, cross\-referenced between device_id/web_id and user_unique_id, user_unique_id priority is greater than device_id/web_id<br><br>* When generating the ssid, the relationship between the individual IDs is bound.<br><br>   * The relationship between device_id/web_id and ssid is n: n, through device_id/web_id can only find the ssid of the latest binding of the id, and through ssid can only find the device_id/web_id of the latest binding of the ssid<br><br>   * user_unique_id supports multiple classes, the type can be set by user_unique_id_type parameters, and the relationship between each class user_unique_id and ssid can be 1:1 or n: 1 |
|ID isolation granularity |Ssid is isolated at the application (appid) level.<br><br>In the old ID system, the same user_unique_id under an application (appid) correspond to the same ssid, and the same user_unique_id correspond to different ssid under different applications (appid) |ssid is isolated at the group level. That is, multiple application SDs under the group can be uniformly identified and managed. |
|Logical comparison |* Application scenario: Implement the concatenation of users from anonymity to real name and from real name to anonymity through ssid.<br><br>* Limitations: user_unique_id has no clear meaning, and is only allowed to be set to a business ID, can not support multi\-caliber, multi\-business scenario data can not get through.<br><br>   For example, the app of a bank customer has integrated the SDK of data access to collect behavioral data, and user_unique_id set to the customer number. The user's login form also includes the registration of untied cards. At this time, the customer number cannot be obtained, but the mobile phone number can be obtained. However, due to the fact that other types of business IDs cannot be carried when reporting, the relevant event data generated can only be recorded as anonymous. Therefore, the customer's demand for sending card\-tied text messages to the user through the mobile phone number cannot be met. |* Advantages: Support unified user identification in multi\-application (subject) and multi\-caliber scenarios. |

## Example 2: Global association identity


* Example scenario

   A bank customer's App requires SDK integrated data access for behavioral data collection, the user can obtain the device number when not registered, use the device number to report anonymous data, the user can obtain the mobile phone number after registration, and take the mobile phone number to report real\-name data, the user can obtain the relationship between the card number and the mobile phone number after tying the card, and use the card number to report transaction data at the server level, while the customer also has a WeChat Mini Program, from WeChat Mini Program You can get the Mini Program union_id, using union_id in the WeChat Mini Program to report.

* User user_unique_id Type Settings (Multi\-Aperture Settings)

   
   |Business ID |Whether to force 1:1 with ssid |Offline real\-time relationship |user_unique_id_type |
   |---|---|---|---|
   |Card number |Yes |Real\-time is higher than offline |card_id |
   |Mobile phone number |Yes |Offline is higher than real\-time |phone_id |
   |Mini Program union_id |No |Offline is higher than real\-time |union_id |
   |Device number |No |Only real\-time input |device_id |
   

* User behavior data reporting example

   \*\*Yesterday's \*\*user behavior data report

   
   |Example Scenario 1: **Yesterday** User Behavior Data Report |Example scenario 2: **Today** offline id\-mapping & user behavior data reporting |
   |---|---|
   |1. The user downloads and uses the app, uses device_id to report anonymous events, and an **e1** event occurs. At this time, there are device_id1, device_id1 has not bound any ssid, and a new ssid1 is generated as the ssid of e1<br><br>2. The user registers and logs in, uses device_id and phone_id to report the real\-name event, the behavior before and after the series anonymity, the **e2** event occurs, there are device_id1 and phone_id1, phone_id1 unbound ssid, device_id1 bound ssid1, ssid1 unbound phone_id, so use ssid1 as the ssid of e2, and bind ssid1 and phone_id1 to each other<br><br>3. User binding card number, can get the relationship between card_id and phone_id, so use **id_bind** binding card_id and phone_id, at this time there are phone_id1 and card_id1, card_id1 not bound to ssid, phone_id1 bound to ssid1, ssid1 is not bound to card_id, so the card_id1 and ssid1 bound to each other<br><br>4. The user reports the payment behavior using the server level, and the **e3** event occurs. At this time, there is card_id1, card_id1 is bound to ssid1, so ssid1 is used as the ssid of e3<br><br>5. Another device downloads and uses the app, uses device_id to report anonymous events, and an **e4** event occurs. At this time, there are device_id2, device_id2 has not bound any ssid, and a new ssid2 is generated as the ssid of e4<br><br>6. The user authorizes the mobile phone number in the Mini Program, gets the phone_id1, calls the **id_bind** interface to bind union_id1 and phone_id1, phone_id1 has bound ssid1, so union_id1 is also bound to ssid1<br><br>8. The user continues to use the Mini Program, and the **e6** event occurs. At this time, there are union_id1 and device_id2, union_id1 bound to ssid1, so ssid1 is used as the ssid of e6, and device_id2 and ssid1 are bound to each other |8. **Today's** offline id\-mapping:<br><br>   Offline id\-mapping, assuming phone_id1 bound to ssid3, since phoine_id offline priority is higher than real\-time, phone_id1 will be rebounded to ssid3 and written to real\-time id\-mapping, real\-time id\-mapping phone_id1 bound to ssid3<br><br>9. **Today's** user behavior data report:<br><br>   In the login scenario, the e7 event occurs, there are device_id1 and phone_id1, phone_id1 bound ssid3, so use ssid3 as the ssid of e7 |

# **Anonymity and real\-name recognition logic**

The system generates an internal statistical caliber SSID (user) based on the visitor's device and the visitor's ID. In the case of the same device ID, when a user registers and logs in, the system will assign the user the same SSID as when they were not logged in anonymously, thus ensuring that the user's behavior before and after logging in belongs to the same person.

Specific examples are as follows:


| |**device_id** |**user_unique_id** |**ssid** |**Remarks** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Device A\-Anonymous |A | |ssid1 | |
|Device A\-Registration |A |123 |ssid1 |The ssid remains unchanged before and after the new user registers on the same device |
|Device A\-Logout |A | |ssid1 | |
|Device A \- Switch User |A |234 |ssid2 |After the user switches, a new ssid is generated. |
| | | | | |
|Device B \- Anonymous |B | |ssid3 |New device generates new ssid |
|Device B\-Login |B |123 |ssid1 |Log in to the old user with the new device, and the ssid will take the ssid corresponding to the previous uuid.<br><br><div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-tips-is-title="true">tip</div><br><br><br><br>* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">If you are using a private environment and the multi\-device correction function is enabled, after 123 users log into device B, the ssid in the anonymous scenario will be corrected from ssid3 to ssid1.</div><br><br><br>* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">SaaS\-like environments do not support multi\-device fixes.</div><br> |
|Device B \- Switch User |B |234 |ssid2 | |
|Device B \- Registration |B |345 |ssid4 |Regenerate ssid for new registered users |
| | | | | |
|history import user | |789 |ssid5 | |
|Device C\-Anonymous |C | |ssid6 | |
|Device C\-login |C |789 |ssid5 | |


<span id="3a98e04f"></span>
# **Identification logic for new and old users**

The system provides a virtual user attribute "user_is_new", which can be used to determine whether one of the first event date saved in the user attribute and the selected time at the time of analysis is the same day to determine whether the user is a new user on that day.

<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-tips-is-title="true">tip</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">The statistical caliber of the DataFinder's default user ID is ssid, so the statistical caliber of the user attribute "user_is_new" is also ssid.</div>


Examples are as follows:

The date corresponding to the first event time recorded in the attributes of user A is August 1. If the analyzed event occurs on August 3, user A will be counted as an old user on August 3. Similarly, if the analyzed event occurs on August 1, user A will be counted as a new user on August 1.

<span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/7203a20dfa194dd58cac1a89f9063f47~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>

<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true">warning</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">If there is a scene of importing a batch of historical users from your own database, you need to call the set_profile interface to update the time of the user's real first event to the user attribute "first event time" to ensure the accuracy of the statistical results of new and old users.</div>


In addition, DataFinder also provides whether the first day of access ($is_first_day) attribute, new and old users (user_is_new) and whether the first day of access ($is_first_day) are based on the user attribute activation time (first_event_time, SaaS\-cloud\-native and privatized environment) to calculate, the main difference is that the former is affected by the selected time period, while the latter is not affected, so the latter in different chart types get better consistency of calculation results.


* First day visit ($is_first_day): The target event and the first event occurred on the same day.

* user_is_new: The target event and the first event occur in the same cycle. For example, in a bar chart, the period is the time frame selected by the user.


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true">warning</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">For data analytics:</div>



* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">It is recommended <strong>to use whether first day access ($is_first_day)</strong> to determine new and old users.</div>


* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">Only new and old users (user_is_new) can be used in DataFinder's advanced analysis, and other scenarios try to <strong>not directly use new and old users (user_is_new)</strong> , the data may not meet user expectations.</div>


* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">If you need to set the time range flexibly, you can also use the user attribute activation time (first_event_time, SaaS\-cloud\-native, privatized environment).</div>



For more logical comparisons and introductions of the two, see [New and existing users/whether it is relevant on the first day](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Statistical_Criteria_Value_Logic#3dac52c5).
